q1.prompt: You need the value at index i in a collection of n elements. Which shape makes that jump cheap?

choices.label: Array — address is base + i * width
Linked list — walk from the head each time

wrong_list_for_index.prompt: A list still pays O(i) to reach index i.
wrong_list_for_index.explanation: Index access on a linked list walks i nodes. An array computes the address in O(1).

q2.prompt: You already hold a pointer to a node and must splice it out of a chain. Which shape keeps that edit local?

choices.label: Linked list — relink neighbors in O(1)
Array — shift the tail after the hole

wrong_array_for_splice.prompt: An array still shifts the tail.
wrong_array_for_splice.explanation: Splicing in the middle of an array moves every later element. A linked list rewires pointers when you already hold the node.

success.prompt: You matched array to index jumps and list to local splices.
